name: Tobias
waitingLines: I’ll wait for {partner}. No rush. I’ve got all the time in the world. Literally.
Saving a seat for {partner}. I’m comfortable. Very comfortable. No rush.

questions.scene: Tobias pulls out a small photo of a very old tortoise.
lines: He's a hero of mine. Old friend. No rush.
questions.question: Who is Jonathan the tortoise?

choices.label: The oldest known living land animal
reply: Correct. A legend.
Jonathan is a giant tortoise believed to have hatched around 1832.
He's lived through so much. Still eats his greens.

choices.label: A famous racing tortoise
reply: Racing? Oh, no. He walks.
He's believed to be the oldest living land animal.
Hatched around 1832. Still going. No rush.

choices.label: A tortoise who starred in movies
reply: Not quite. Although he's famous.
He's the oldest known living land animal.
Nearly two centuries old. Puts my slow pace in perspective.

questions.factBasis: Jonathan, a Seychelles giant tortoise, is the oldest known living land animal (hatched c. 1832).

questions.scene: Tobias gazes at a photo of a golden aspen forest, utterly peaceful.
lines: That whole forest might be one tree. No rush. Let it sink in.
questions.question: What's special about Pando, a grove of aspen trees in Utah?

choices.label: It's made of fake plastic trees
reply: Oh, no. Very real. Very old.
It's a single organism with one shared root system.
Possibly thousands of years old. A patient giant.

choices.label: The trees walk around slowly
reply: Like me? Lovely thought. No.
It's one organism connected by a single root system.
One of the heaviest living things on Earth. Quietly.

choices.label: It's one single organism sharing one root system
reply: Correct. One giant family under the soil.
Tens of thousands of trunks all grow from the same roots.
Connected underground, like old friends. I find that very moving.

questions.factBasis: Pando is a clonal colony of quaking aspen sharing one root system.

questions.scene: Tobias gestures to a fuzzy green plant hanging from your ceiling.
lines: Another slow friend. I admire him. No rush.
questions.question: What grows on a sloth's fur because it moves so slowly?

choices.label: Flowers
reply: How lovely. Not quite.
It's algae, giving sloths a green tint.
Camouflage by being patient. I respect that.

choices.label: Moss
reply: Close. It's actually algae.
Algae grows in their fur and tints it green.
A whole ecosystem on one sleepy animal.

choices.label: Algae
reply: Correct. A tiny garden.
Sloth fur can host algae, which gives it a greenish tint.
Helps them blend in with the trees. Slow and stylish.

questions.factBasis: Sloth fur hosts algae (and other organisms).

questions.scene: A butterfly lands on Tobias's foot. He doesn't move. For a very, very long time.
lines: She's tasting me. That's how they taste. No rush. I'll wait.
questions.question: How do butterflies taste things?

choices.label: With their wings
reply: A pretty idea. Not quite.
They taste with sensors on their feet.
So landing is tasting. Very efficient lunch planning.

choices.label: With sensors on their feet
reply: Correct. Toes for tasting.
Butterflies taste plants by standing on them.
Imagine tasting your salad by stepping in it. Marlow said no.

choices.label: They can't taste at all
reply: Oh, they can. Just differently.
Their taste sensors are on their feet.
Very curious feet. Respect.

questions.factBasis: Butterflies have taste receptors (chemoreceptors) on their feet.

questions.scene: Tobias looks at a bamboo stalk on your shelf with deep respect.
lines: Patience is a plant, sometimes.
questions.question: How often do some bamboo species flower?

choices.label: Once every 100 years or more
reply: Correct. Remarkable.
Some species flower all at the same time, decades apart.
That's my kind of timeline.

choices.label: Every spring
reply: Oh, much rarer than that.
Some bamboo species flower only once every 100 years or more.
And often all at once, across the world. Synchronized patience.

choices.label: Never
reply: They do. Just very rarely.
Some bamboo flowers only once every 100+ years.
Worth waiting for. Like Marlow saying yes.

questions.factBasis: Some bamboo species (e.g., Phyllostachys bambusoides) flower at ~120-year intervals.

questions.scene: Tobias peeks into a hole in your garden, delighted.
lines: Being a good neighbor matters. No rush.
questions.question: How many other species can use a gopher tortoise's burrow?

choices.label: Just one, the tortoise
reply: Oh, it's much more crowded than that.
Over 350 species use gopher tortoise burrows.
Frogs, snakes, mice, owls. A whole apartment complex.

choices.label: Over 350
reply: Correct. Wonderful.
Gopher tortoise burrows shelter more than 350 other species.
Generous hosts. Marlow says I'm the same with snacks.

choices.label: About 10
reply: More than that. Many more.
Over 350 species have been found using them.
The best landlord in the forest. No rent.

questions.factBasis: Gopher tortoise burrows are used by 350+ other species.

questions.scene: Tobias writes 'thank you' on a tiny note and slides it across the table, very slowly.
lines: Marlow and I do this. Small thanks. Every day. For years.
questions.question: What does research suggest about expressing gratitude to a partner?

choices.label: It helps couples feel more connected and committed
reply: Correct. Gratitude is glue.
Feeling appreciated makes both partners more invested in each other.
Small thanks. Every day. That's the whole secret.

choices.label: It makes partners take you for granted
reply: Oh, no. The opposite.
Gratitude is linked to feeling closer and more committed.
Say thank you. Slowly. Mean it.

choices.label: It only matters on anniversaries
reply: Every ordinary day counts.
Regular gratitude helps couples stay connected.
Tiny thanks pile up into something big.

questions.factBasis: Algoe et al.: expressing gratitude predicts relationship maintenance and connection.

questions.scene: Tobias admires a spiky agave plant on your windowsill.
lines: About waiting for something big. No rush.
questions.question: Why is the agave sometimes called a 'century plant'?

choices.label: It grows exactly 100 leaves
reply: Clever guess. Not it.
It can take decades to bloom, then flowers once.
Not quite a century, but a very long wait.

choices.label: It lives for exactly 100 years
reply: Close in spirit. Not exactly.
It blooms once after many years, then usually dies.
One big moment. Worth the wait.

choices.label: It takes decades to bloom, then blooms once
reply: Correct. Beautiful.
It grows for decades, then sends up one giant flower stalk.
Patient, then spectacular. My ideal life plan.

questions.factBasis: Agave americana ('century plant') blooms once after 10–30+ years.

questions.scene: Tobias slowly chews a slice of watermelon. Juice drips. He is unbothered.
lines: Very refreshing. Mostly water. Like me after a bath. No rush.
questions.question: About how much of a watermelon is water?

choices.label: About 10%
reply: Oh, much juicier than that.
Watermelon is about 92% water.
It's practically a drink you can chew.

choices.label: About 92%
reply: Correct. Almost all water.
That's why it's so refreshing on hot days.
Best eaten slowly, in the shade, with someone you love.

choices.label: About 50%
reply: More. Much more.
It's roughly 92% water.
Nature's slow-sipping snack.

questions.scene: Tobias watches a chicken peck around the yard with deep respect.
lines: That's a dinosaur. A small one. I knew it all along. Slowly.
questions.question: Which living animals are actually dinosaurs?

choices.label: Crocodiles
reply: Close cousins. Not dinosaurs themselves.
The real living dinosaurs are birds.
They evolved from small, feathered dinosaurs long ago.

choices.label: Birds
reply: Correct. Birds are dinosaurs.
They descend from small feathered dinosaurs.
So that chicken is a distant cousin of T. rex. Treat it with respect.

choices.label: Tortoises
reply: Oh, flattering. But no.
Birds are the living dinosaurs.
I'm old. Not that old.

questions.scene: Tobias takes a very slow sip of tea.
lines: I chased Marlow for three years. Slowly. Very slowly.
questions.question: Your love story pace: slow burn, or whirlwind?

choices.label: Slow burn
reply: Slow burn. Oh, the best kind.
Warm, steady, built to last.

choices.label: Whirlwind
reply: Whirlwind. Oh, my. Exciting.
Hold on to your hat.

A:A: Slow burn for both of you. No rush, indeed.
So you and {partner} took your time. And look at you now.
Savor it. Every step.
A:B: Whirlwind for you. {partner} says slow burn.
You were already in love. They were still saying 'let's see.'
Patience paid off. For both of you.
B:A: Slow burn for you. {partner} says whirlwind.
They were spinning. You were... considering.
Funny how both of you ended up in the same place.
B:B: Whirlwind for both of you. Oh, my.
I can just picture it: {partner} and you said 'I love you' in week two.
Dizzying. Wonderful. Hold hands so you don't fall.

questions.scene: Tobias gazes out the window at a lazy sunrise.
lines: Mornings are my favorite. They come every day. No rush.
questions.question: Sunday morning: sleep in, or an early walk?

choices.label: Sleep in
reply: Sleep in. Wise.
Sleep is a skill. You're a master.

choices.label: Early walk
reply: Early walk. Oh, energy.
Dew on the grass. Birds saying hello.

A:A: Sleep in, both of you. Perfect.
Honestly, you and {partner} wake up when you wake up. No alarms.
Pancakes at noon. My kind of Sunday.
A:B: You walk early. {partner} sleeps in.
Bring them coffee when you get back. Gently wake them.
A sunrise for you. A warm cup for them.
B:A: You sleep in. {partner} walks early.
They'll be back with croissants before you open your eyes.
That's a wonderful arrangement, really.
B:B: Early walks, both of you. Wonderful.
Something tells me {partner} and you greet the sunrise together.
Bring warm drinks. Walk slowly. Very slowly.

questions.scene: Tobias opens a dusty box full of keepsakes, one item at a time.
lines: I keep everything. Marlow's first note. A leaf from our first walk.
questions.question: Favorite keepsake: old photos, old letters, or a playlist of 'our songs'?

choices.label: Old photos
reply: Old photos. Time in a frame.
Faces and moments, kept still.

choices.label: Old letters
reply: Old letters. Ink and heart.
Words that waited to be reread.

choices.label: A playlist of 'our songs'
reply: A playlist. Melodies remember.
One song, one memory.

A:A: Photos for both of you. Lovely.
Make an album with {partner}. One page a year.
Fill it slowly. No rush.
A:B: Letters for you. {partner} loves photos.
Tuck one small photo inside every letter you write them.
A keepsake inside a keepsake. Very efficient sentiment.
A:C: Put on your songs and flip through the albums together.
A soundtrack for every memory. Take your time. Every page.
B:A: Photos for you. {partner} treasures letters.
Write a little caption on the back of each photo. Now it's both.
Marlow does this. Her captions are funnier than the photos.
B:B: Letters for both of you. Beautiful.
You and {partner} probably have a ribbon-tied stack somewhere.
Write a new one. Add it to the pile.
B:C: Playlist for you. {partner} keeps the letters.
Read their letters out loud while your songs play softly.
That's a perfect evening. Slow. Warm. No rush at all.
C:A: Photos for you. {partner} keeps the playlist.
Make a slideshow and set it to 'your songs.'
Watch it on a rainy evening. Bring tissues. Several.
C:B: Letters for you. {partner} loves a playlist.
Handwrite the one lyric that always reminds you of them.
They'll hear that song differently forever. That's the plan.
C:C: Playlists for both of you. Musical hearts.
So {partner} and you probably have a song for every season.
Play it on a long drive. Hold hands.

questions.scene: Tobias turns a small wrapped gift over and over, slowly.
lines: Gifts. I take weeks to choose them. Marlow says it's worth it. No rush.
questions.question: Gifts: something useful, or something sentimental?

choices.label: Something useful
reply: Useful. Practical love.
A gift you'll use every day.

choices.label: Something sentimental
reply: Sentimental. Oh, tender.
A gift you'll keep forever.

A:A: Useful gifts for both of you. Practical hearts.
{partner} gives you a good umbrella. You give them warm socks.
Love you can use.
A:B: Sentimental for you. {partner} likes useful.
Engrave something they'll use every single day.
A mug with your words on it. They'll think of you every sip.
B:A: Useful for you. {partner} loves sentimental.
Give them something practical and tuck a handwritten note inside.
An umbrella that says 'I'll keep you dry.' Practical poetry.
B:B: Sentimental gifts for both of you.
I can just picture it: you and {partner} have a drawer full of meaningful little things.
Keep every one. Even the tiny ones.

questions.scene: Tobias pours two cups of tea and sets one across from him.
lines: Small rituals are big things. No rush.
questions.question: A ritual you'd keep forever: morning coffee together, or an evening walk?

choices.label: Morning coffee together
reply: Morning coffee. Lovely start.
Two cups. One conversation.

choices.label: An evening walk
reply: Evening walk. Lovely end.
Streetlights, quiet talks, slow steps.

A:A: Morning coffee for both of you.
Every day starts with {partner} across the table.
Forty years from now, same cups. Same love.
A:B: Evening walk for you. {partner} wants morning coffee.
Start with coffee. End with a walk.
A whole day held between two little rituals.
B:A: Morning coffee for you. {partner} wants evening walks.
Coffee at dawn. Walk at dusk. Bookends of the day.
Two rituals. Twice the love.
B:B: Evening walks for both of you.
Honestly, {partner} and you will know every tree in the neighborhood.
Slow steps. Long talks. Perfect.

questions.scene: Tobias ponders slowly, tapping two claws together.
lines: I took three years to ask Marlow out. I'm still deciding if that was too fast.
questions.question: How does your partner make big decisions?
questions.selfQuestion: How do you make big decisions?

choices.label: Quickly, on instinct
reply: Quickly, on instinct. Remarkable.
I once took a week to pick a lettuce.

choices.label: Takes a week
reply: Takes a week. A kindred spirit.
Time is the best advisor. And it's free.

choices.label: Asks everyone they know
reply: Asks everyone. Very democratic.
The group chat votes. The heart decides.

A:A: Quick on instinct, and {partner} knew it.
They know you decide before they've finished asking the question.
I find that thrilling. From a safe distance.
A:B: You take a week. {partner} guessed instant instinct.
They're tapping their foot on day two. You're on day two of seven.
Tell them 'no rush' in advance. It's my favorite phrase.
A:C: You ask everyone. {partner} thought you'd just go with your gut.
They don't know about the five friends you texted.
Add them to the poll. First. Before your aunt.
B:A: You decide fast. {partner} guessed you'd take a week.
They're patiently waiting while you've already bought the thing.
Tell them gently. They were preparing to be patient.
B:B: A full week, and {partner} knew it.
They've learned to ask on Monday and expect an answer next Monday.
That's not slowness. That's craftsmanship.
B:C: You ask everyone. {partner} thought you'd quietly mull it over.
They imagine you thinking alone. You're in four group chats.
Next time, ask them first. Their vote should count double.
C:A: You decide fast. {partner} guessed you'd poll everyone.
They're expecting a group chat survey. You just... chose.
Bold. Very un-tortoise. I respect it from afar.
C:B: You take a week. {partner} guessed you'd ask everyone.
They think you're consulting friends. You're consulting the ceiling.
Quiet thinking is still thinking. Marlow taught me to say it out loud.
C:C: They know your group chat has opinions on your couch, your haircut, and them.
Wise. Many voices. Just make sure theirs counts double.

questions.scene: Tobias settles into an imaginary line, perfectly content. He could stay here for years.
lines: Waiting is an art form. I'm a master. Ask anyone. Slowly.
questions.question: While waiting in a long line, what does your partner do?
questions.selfQuestion: While waiting in a long line, what do you do?

choices.label: Chats with strangers
reply: Chats with strangers. A friend-maker.
By the front of the line, they're invited to a wedding.

choices.label: People-watches quietly
reply: People-watches quietly. A fine pastime.
Every line is a small theater.

A:A: Chatting with strangers, and {partner} knew it.
They know you'll know the life story of the person ahead by the time you order.
Charming. Exhausting to watch. But charming.
A:B: You people-watch. {partner} expected you to chat everyone up.
They're waiting for small talk. You're silently narrating a documentary.
Whisper your theories to them. Best line date ever.
B:A: You chat. {partner} expected you to quietly people-watch.
Plot twist: you're the social one. They've misjudged you for years.
Introduce them to your new line friends. All of them.
B:B: People-watching, and {partner} knew it.
They know you're inventing quiet backstories for everyone in line.
'He's a retired pirate.' Yes. Same hobby. Welcome.

questions.scene: Tobias lights a small candle. It takes him a while. He's proud when it works.
lines: Romance lives in the small things. Most things do.
questions.question: What would your partner call the most romantic gesture?
questions.selfQuestion: What would you call the most romantic gesture?

choices.label: A handwritten note
reply: A handwritten note. Ink and heart.
Something they can keep in a drawer forever.

choices.label: Remembering a tiny detail
reply: Remembering a tiny detail. Oh, yes.
How they take their tea. Which side they sleep on.

A:A: A handwritten note, and {partner} knew it.
They know paper and ink mean everything to you.
Write them one tonight. Slowly. Mean every word.
A:B: Details move you. {partner} guessed a handwritten note.
They're writing paragraphs. You just want them to remember your favorite mug.
Tell them one detail you love that they remember. They'll glow.
B:A: A note moves you. {partner} guessed tiny details.
They've been memorizing your coffee order. You've wanted a letter.
Ask for one. Or write them a note about the details. Combo.
B:B: Tiny details, and {partner} knew it.
They know you melt when they remember the little things.
Marlow remembers I like my lettuce slightly wilted. I nearly proposed.

questions.scene: Tobias chuckles softly, remembering something from long ago. Possibly last week.
lines: It took me a long time to realize I liked Marlow. About a year. Then two more to say it.
questions.question: How long did it take your partner to realize they liked you?
questions.selfQuestion: How long did it take you to realize you liked your partner?

choices.label: Right away
reply: Right away. Oh, how lovely.
One look and they were done for.

choices.label: Embarrassingly long
reply: Embarrassingly long. Oh, my people.
The heart knew. The brain needed a memo.

A:A: Right away, and {partner} knew it.
They knew you were smitten from the very first hello.
Lovely. Simple. Some hearts just know. Mine needed a calendar.
A:B: It took you ages. {partner} thought it was instant.
They thought you fell immediately. You were still... processing.
No rush. You got there. That's what matters.
B:A: You knew right away. {partner} thought it took you ages.
They think they had to win you over. You were already won.
Tell them. They'll smile for a week. Maybe two.
B:B: Embarrassingly long, and {partner} knew it.
They watched you slowly figure it out. Patiently. Possibly with popcorn.
Worth the wait. Slow-cooked love tastes best.

questions.scene: Tobias watches the sun rise through your curtains. He has been watching since 4 a.m.
lines: Mornings. My favorite. They come every day, and I'm grateful every time.
questions.question: How does your partner start a slow morning?
questions.selfQuestion: How do you start a slow morning?

choices.label: Up with the sun
reply: Up with the sun. A fellow early riser.
Birds and them, the first ones awake.

choices.label: Snoozes five times
reply: Snoozes five times. Very human.
Five more minutes, times five.

A:A: Up with the sun, and {partner} knew it.
They know you're greeting the day while they're still dreaming.
Make them tea. Leave it by the bed. Quietly.
A:B: You snooze. {partner} guessed you'd be up with the sun.
They imagined a sunrise person. They got a pillow person.
Snooze one less time this week. A small gift for them.
B:A: Up with the sun for you. {partner} guessed snoozing.
They think you're asleep. You've been up for hours, watering plants.
Bring them breakfast. Prove it.
B:B: Five snoozes, and {partner} knew it.
They know the alarm is more of a suggestion to you.
Sleep is precious. Snooze with dignity. No rush.
